h1: The 6 Best Infrared Patio Heaters of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Infrared Patio Heaters 2026: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 6 infrared patio heaters compared on wattage, voltage, mounting, weather rating and and coverage.
summary: The Hykolity 1500W wall-mount is the best heater for most patios, with IP55 weatherproofing, ETL certification and a 24 hour timer. The DR. INFRARED 1500W is the plug-in with the most mounting flexibility, the DR-239 steps up to 3000W on a 240V plug, and the Infratech WD-6024 is the professional choice for big covered areas.
intro: Infrared patio heaters get compared by watts, and watts hide the part that matters most: where the heat goes. Infrared warms people and objects directly, so a heater aimed right on a 1500W setting can beat a 3000W one pointing at the wrong spot. Mounting height and angle decide how much of that power lands on your seat.

We ranked six infrared heaters from the listings: wattage and voltage, mounting options, weather rating, certification, controls and coverage claims. The big ones need 240V power, often hardwired, which is a job for an electrician. Infrared heaters need a clear line to the people they warm, and they need a safe clearance from ceilings and awnings, so read each installation limit.

products.name: Hykolity 35.5 Inch 1500W Infrared Wall Mount Patio Heater
products.verdict: A 35.5 inch 1500W dual-tube wall mount rated IP55, ETL certified, with three power levels and a 24 hour timer.
products.description:
The Hykolity uses 1500W dual carbon tubes, an IP55 weatherproof body, ETL certification, three power levels and a 24 hour timer, in a 35.5 inch wall-mount form.

It ranks first because certification and weatherproofing come with the controls most people need: low, medium and high, plus a timer. It outranks the DR. INFRARED 1500W because the wall mount is better for an uncovered location, but it cannot be moved around. The Kihdockood has a better water rating and eight heat levels.

Buy it if the heater lives in one spot on an exposed patio. Skip it if you want to move it between rooms. Mount it on a stud or masonry wall.
products.idealFor: Uncovered locations where IP55 and ETL matter.

products.name: Kihdockood 41 Inch 1500W IP65 Infrared Patio Heater
products.verdict: A 41 inch 1500W heater with eight heat levels, IP65 and a 45 degree tilt.
products.description:
The Kihdockood is a 41 inch 1500W infrared heater with eight heat levels, an IP65 waterproof rating and a bracket that angles the heater up to 45 degrees.

It ranks second because aiming is the difference between warm and wasted, and eight levels add fine control. IP65 is a step above the Hykolity's IP55. It loses on listed certification, which the page does not state.

Buy it if you need to aim heat at a seating group. Skip it if ETL certification is a requirement. Aim it before you add the furniture.
products.idealFor: Seating groups where aiming heat matters.

products.name: DR. INFRARED 1500W Portable Infrared Patio Heater
products.verdict: A 1500W plug-in with 900, 1200 and 1500W settings, 3-way mounting and a 12 hour timer.
products.description:
The DR. INFRARED has 900, 1200 and 1500W settings, a 3-way mounting option of freestanding, wall or ceiling, a weighted base with wheels, ETL certification and a 12 hour timer.

It ranks third because freestanding use is rare here, so it wins on flexibility, but 1500W on a standard plug is the limit of a small porch. It trails the Hykolity on weather rating, which the listing does not state.

Buy it if you want to move the heater or try different mounts. Skip it if you want a documented waterproof rating. Keep it dry in winter storage.
products.idealFor: Small porches that want plug-in infrared.
products.skipIf: You need a stated weather rating.

products.name: DR. INFRARED DR-239 3000W Wall or Ceiling Infrared Heater
products.verdict: A 3000W, 10,260 BTU heater on 220V to 240V with IP55 and a remote.
products.description:
The DR-239 is a 3000W heater at 10,260 BTU on 220V to 240V with a NEMA 6-15P plug, IP55 weatherproofing, ETL listing and a remote.

It ranks fourth because double the wattage covers more seats, but it needs a 240V outlet, which most patios lack. It beats the 1500W models on power and loses on ease of install.

Buy it if you have a 240V outlet. Skip it if you only have standard 120V power. Confirm the outlet type before buying.

products.name: ThermoMate 4500W Carbon Fiber Infrared Patio Heater
products.verdict: A 4500W hardwired 240V heater with three power levels, IP54 and a 45 degree tilt.
products.description:
The ThermoMate is a 4500W carbon fiber heater, hardwired at 240V, with 2250W, 3600W and 4500W levels, IP54 and a 45 degree tilt. The listing claims coverage up to about 200 sq ft and a mounting height of at least 7.88 ft.

It ranks fifth because hardwiring and the mounting height make it a project, not a purchase. The IP54 rating is the lowest weather rating of the group, though adequate under cover.

Buy it if you have a large covered deck with a high ceiling. Skip it if you have no electrician or a low roof. Check the ceiling height before ordering.
products.idealFor: Large porches and decks with high ceilings.
products.skipIf: You rent or have a low ceiling.

products.name: Infratech WD-6024 6000W 240V Stainless Infrared Heater
products.verdict: A 6000W 240V stainless heater, 61.25 inches long, UL/CUL listed with a 3-year warranty.
products.description:
The Infratech WD-6024 is 6000W at 240V, 61.25 inches long, made of 304 stainless steel, UL/CUL listed with a 3-year warranty.

It ranks last for homeowners because it needs professional installation and costs more, yet it is the most robust. The 3-year warranty is the longest stated in the group.

Buy it if you run a large covered patio or commercial space. Skip it if you want a plug-in. Plan on a professional install.
products.idealFor: Large covered patios and commercial spaces.

whatMatters.detail: Watts measure heat output, and voltage tells you the outlet you need. 1500W models run on standard 120V, while 3000W and above use 240V. Check the voltage and plug type on the listing, and ask an electrician about 240V circuits before ordering. Match the wattage to the number of people you want to warm, and remember that wind steals heat from any setting.

The IP rating shows dust and water protection. IP54 handles splashes, IP55 handles water jets, and IP65 sits a step above. Check the rating on the listing if the heater sees rain, and install under at least partial cover for longevity. Look for the ratings line in the spec table, because marketing copy often says waterproof without a number.

Infrared works by line of sight, so mount height and angle determine who gets warmed. A tilting wall mount, like the Kihdockood's 45 degrees, aims heat at a seat. Check the height guidance on the listing, which can be at least 7.88 ft. Keep clearances from awnings and ceilings as stated in the manual.

ETL and UL/CUL listings mean a lab tested the heater to a safety standard. It matters for a device that gets hot near a ceiling. Check for a listing mark in the specs, and avoid unlisted heaters near awnings. A listing mark also helps if your insurer asks about installed heaters.

Power levels let you drop from 1500W to a lower setting when it is not cold. A timer shuts the heater off if you forget. Check the number of levels and timer length on the listing, with 12 or 24 hours in this group. A timer is cheap insurance against leaving a heater running overnight.

faq.q: Can I install a hardwired heater myself?
faq.a: The ThermoMate and Infratech are hardwired at 240V, which needs a licensed electrician in most places. The DR. INFRARED 1500W plugs in, so it needs no wiring. A professional also checks the circuit breaker size.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake?
faq.a: Mounting it too high or pointing it wrong. Infrared warms what it hits, so the Kihdockood's 45 degree tilt matters more than a spare few watts. Check the height guidance. Aiming is half the battle, so plan seating around the heater.

faq.q: Is the DR-239 worth it over a 1500W model?
faq.a: If you have 240V power, yes. The DR-239 gives 3000W and 10,260 BTU with a remote, but a 1500W Hykolity does well for one seating spot. A remote also saves a cold walk to the switch.

faq.q: How do I install a wall mount?
faq.a: Screw the bracket into a stud or masonry at the stated height, hang the heater and set the tilt. The Hykolity and Kihdockood are wall-mount models, so check the wall can carry them. Check the mounting height before drilling anything.

faq.q: How should I look after it?
faq.a: Dust the tubes when cool and check the mount for loosening each season. A stainless body like the Infratech's 304 steel resists corrosion best. Wipe the housing after storms.

faq.q: Do infrared heaters work in wind?
faq.a: Better than propane, since infrared warms people directly instead of the air. Strong gusts still cool you, so place the heater near a wall or screen. A wall or screen behind you reflects heat back.

finalTake: The Hykolity 1500W wall-mount heater is the best heater for most patios, with IP55, ETL and a 24 hour timer. Choose the Kihdockood for aiming, the DR. INFRARED for a movable plug-in, and the DR-239 if you have 240V. Hire an electrician for the hardwired models.
